title: CompilerOutput
description: Contract for the normalized output of the PromptForge compiler model. This schema is embedded in the compiler system prompt and is what the model must produce. It deliberately contains NO client-owned identifiers: task_id, project_id and schema_version are assigned by the client during enrichment and must not appear here. Unknown fields are rejected. Lifecycle: raw provider response → JSON extraction & normalization → validation against THIS schema → optional bounded repair (max 1) → client enrichment → validation against taskspec.schema.json → profile-aware rendering → persistence. See docs/TASKSPEC.md.

task_type.description: Classification of the requested work. Drives context-selection heuristics.

execution_mode.description: Resolved depth of this compilation. The UI-level 'auto' value is resolved before compilation and never appears here.

target_model.description: The AI model that will execute the task (e.g. 'deepseek-v4-pro', 'qwen-3.8-max', 'gpt-5.6-sol', 'opus-5'). This is the model identity, not the coding runtime.

agent_runtime.description: The coding agent/runtime that will execute the task. Determines which instruction file(s) and renderer family to use. AGENTS.md is shared across all runtimes; runtime-specific instruction files (QWEN.md, CLAUDE.md) are separate.

execution_profile.description: Declarative profile key (e.g. 'deepseek-v4-pro-claude-code') that adapts working style — planning depth, exploration budget, context reuse, reasoning effort, test strategy, retry budget, progress verbosity, autonomy, guardrail strength. Profiles adapt HOW the agent works, never WHAT the task means. The task meaning is identical across all profiles.

objective.description: One explicit sentence describing the outcome the coding agent must achieve.

user_value.description: Why this task matters to the user or product. Optional but encouraged.

current_state.description: Known facts about the project's current state that are material to this task. Facts only, no assumptions.

relevant_context.description: Repository-relative file paths the agent should read before starting (typically .promptforge/context/*.md files). Must only reference context actually supplied with the task.

assumptions.description: Decisions the compiler made without asking, each phrased so the user can veto it. Surfaced verbatim in the rendered prompt.

blocking_questions.description: At most three questions that block correct execution. Only for the product spec's 'must ask' categories (billing provider, data deletion/migration, architecture-changing choices, authorization rules, ambiguous user intent).

scope.description: Concrete, bounded work items the agent must implement.

out_of_scope.description: Explicit exclusions that prevent scope expansion.

requirements.description: Category-grouped requirements. The client pre-fills a missing object with empty arrays during normalization. Empty categories are normal and preferred over invented content.

edge_cases.description: Failure states and boundary conditions the implementation must handle.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable conditions that define completion. Must not be empty.

execution_plan.description: Ordered implementation steps. Expected for 'deep' and 'plan' modes; optional for quick/standard.

test_plan.description: Targeted tests and validation commands the agent should run.

stop_conditions.description: Situations in which the agent must stop and ask instead of proceeding (destructive migrations, production deploys, irreversible operations).

final_report.description: Reporting requirements: items the executing agent must include in its completion report (e.g. changed files, test results, assumptions, remaining risks).

confidence.description: Model self-assessment of specification completeness. Informational only: never rendered as a quality score.

estimated_prompt_tokens.description: Model's own estimate of the rendered prompt size. Advisory only: the client recomputes the estimate locally.
